title: Hiding The Bottom Scoreboard During Replays So Viewers Know It Is Not Live
trigger_condition: Any slow-motion replay or multi-clip highlight package is rolling on screen (CUJ 9.3).
editor_action: Automatically hide the bottom broadcast scorebug the instant a replay wipe starts, and bring the scoreboard back the instant the broadcast returns to the live camera. This keeps the replay picture completely unobstructed and gives viewers a clear visual signal of whether they are watching a replay or live basketball.
timing_constraint: Hide the scoreboard at the start of the replay wipe and restore it immediately upon returning to the live camera (Execute within <= 1.0s reaction window and return to CAM-1 before live ball.)

title: Preserving The '180-Degree Court Line' So Teams Never Appear to Run Backward
trigger_condition: Switching between cameras during live basketball play or immediately after a whistle.
editor_action: Keep all primary live-action cameras (CAM-1, CAM-2, CAM-3 (Player Close-Up)) on the same side of the court. That way, a team attacking from left to right on CAM-1 (Main Wide) still moves from left to right after a camera cut. Never cut to a reverse-side camera during live dribbling, which makes it look like the players suddenly reversed direction; save reverse or overhead CAM-5 (Above-Rim) views for dunks at the rim or labeled slow-motion replays.
timing_constraint: Enforce same-side 180-degree axis continuity on 100% of live-dribbling cuts.
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Tip-In at The Buzzer Finger-Release Frame Freeze
trigger_condition: A player tips a missed shot into the basket right as the period or shot-clock horn sounds.
editor_action: Roll the overhead CAM-5 (Above-Rim) or baseline CAM-2 (Baseline Low) angle and freeze the exact video frame where the backboard LED strip lights up red so viewers can see whether the ball had already left the player's fingertips.
timing_constraint: Hold a 1.5s freeze-frame at the LED light-up frame during the review/halftime window.
plain_english_tip: Two Clocks: Teams have 30 seconds on the shot clock to hit the rim on each possession while the 20-minute half clock counts down.

title: Medical / Gruesome Injury Replay Suppression Rule
trigger_condition: A player suffers a severe ankle roll, knee twist, or head collision and remains down on the court.
editor_action: Show the play at most once at normal speed to explain what happened, or suppress close-up slow-motion loops entirely if the injury is visibly severe, returning to a respectful wide or bench view.
timing_constraint: Zero repeated slow-motion loops on severe lower-body or head injuries (Execute within <= 1.0s reaction window and return to CAM-1 before live ball.)

title: Replay Server Clip-Cue Failure Graceful Abort
trigger_condition: The director calls for a replay during a free-throw gap or timeout, but the replay server stalls on a frozen first frame or fails to roll within 0.8 seconds. (Visual cue: Replay feed frozen or showing the wrong timestamp; Audio cue: Analyst waiting to narrate the replay.)
editor_action: If a queued replay clip does not begin smooth playback within ~0.8 seconds of the transition wipe, immediately dissolve back to live arena cameras (CAM-1 (Main Wide) or CAM-3 (Player Close-Up)) so the broadcast never sits on dead frozen video (example: <= 0.8s replay watchdog timeout). Recommended framing: Main Sideline (CAM-1, Main Wide) or Live Hero Iso (CAM-3, Player Close-Up).
timing_constraint: Target window: <= 0.8s replay watchdog timeout. Re-attempt the replay only on a subsequent stoppage once the clip is verified rolling on preview.
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Entry & Exit Wipe Separation (Clearly Separating Replay Time from Live Action)
trigger_condition: Switching from live action into a recorded slow-motion replay, and returning from the replay back to the live court.
editor_action: Always place a brief visual wipe transition at both the beginning and end of every replay (and hide the live scoreboard during the replay) so someone looking up at the TV never confuses a replay of an earlier basket with a brand-new basket happening live.
timing_constraint: Bracket every replay package with entry/exit stinger wipes and scoreboard suppression (example: 0.3s entry wipe and 0.3s exit wipe).

title: Poster Dunk Dual-Angle Replay (CAM-2 Baseline + CAM-5 Above-Rim)
trigger_condition: A player throws down a powerful one-handed or two-handed dunk over a defender ('poster dunk') followed by a timeout or foul whistle.
editor_action: Roll a back-to-back dual-angle replay package: first CAM-2 (Baseline Low) at 60% speed showing the vertical leap, then CAM-5 (Above-Rim) at 50% speed showing the finish at the rim.
timing_constraint: 6.0s dual-angle replay package during the timeout or free-throw walk-up.
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Saving Exciting Live Plays Silently in The Background (No Interruption)
trigger_condition: An exciting play like a slam dunk, a blocked shot, or a long-distance 3-pointer happens, but the game keeps going without a whistle.
editor_action: Never interrupt live basketball to show a replay while players are still running. Instead, silently save the best close-up camera angles in the background so the clip is ready to play the next time a whistle stops the clock.
timing_constraint: Automatically save a few seconds before and after the highlight in the background while keeping the live wide camera on screen (example: 5s lookback buffer).
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Pacing Replays Across Every 10 Minutes (Never Overwhelming Live Action)
trigger_condition: Macro Game Pattern (Full-Game Replay Budget): Controlling how often slow-motion replays appear over a 10-minute stretch of broadcast time.
editor_action: Keep slow-motion replays to a steady, comfortable rhythm (about 4 to 5 replay segments per 10 minutes of broadcast, or ~10% to 12% of total air time). Use quick single-angle replays during short foul pauses, and save multi-clip highlight packages for the 4 scheduled television timeouts in each half.
timing_constraint: Target roughly 4 to 5 replay segments per 10 minutes of broadcast time so live basketball always remains the star of the show.

title: Automatically Dropping Blocked Camera Angles (Clear Line-Of-Sight Rule)
trigger_condition: A slow-motion replay is about to play after a whistle, and multiple camera angles were saved in the background.
editor_action: Check each saved camera angle before putting it on television: if a referee's back or another player walked right in front of the baseline lens at the moment of the shot or foul, discard that blocked angle and play the clear overhead basket camera (CAM-5, Above-Rim) or high-angle slash camera instead.
timing_constraint: Select only unobstructed camera angles and finish the replay before live play resumes (example: 4.8s clear overhead replay).

title: Holding or Slow-Ramping Replays Until The Analyst Finishes Explaining The Play
trigger_condition: The broadcast analyst is actively breaking down a foul, footwork sequence, or blocked shot while a slow-motion replay (REPLAY-A or REPLAY-B) is on screen.
editor_action: Never cut away from a replay on a rigid timer in the middle of the analyst's sentence if the ball is still dead. Dynamically slow down or briefly pause the replay frame at the exact moment of contact until the analyst finishes explaining why the foul or play happened, unless live play is about to restart.
timing_constraint: Extend or slow-ramp the replay to match the analyst's explanation window, cutting back at least 1.5s before live play resumes (example: 4.5s extended to 6.5s).
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Last-Touch Out-Of-Bounds Finger-Tip Deflection Zoom
trigger_condition: Two players slap at a rebound going out of bounds and argue over whose fingertips touched the ball last.
editor_action: Roll a high-frame-rate 50% speed close-up from CAM-2 (Baseline Low) or REPLAY-B showing the exact direction the basketball's rotation changes off the player's fingertips.
timing_constraint: Roll during the throw-in or monitor review pause (example: 4.0s slow-mo zoom).
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Chase-Down Block Timing Replay
trigger_condition: A defender sprints from behind on a fast break and pins a layup against the backboard.
editor_action: Clip the replay starting 2.5 seconds before the block so viewers see the defender closing the distance downcourt before slowing to 50% speed as the ball hits the glass.
timing_constraint: 100% speed run-up into 50% speed pin at the backboard (example: 4.5s total).
plain_english_tip: Fast Break & Press: Sprinting to score before defenders set up, or guarding full-court immediately after a made basket.

title: 3-Point Shooter Landing-Space Foul Replay
trigger_condition: A defender closes out under a 3-point shooter's feet, not giving the shooter safe room to land.
editor_action: Roll a low-angle slow-motion replay showing both the release at the top of the jump and the defender's foot sliding underneath the shooter's landing spot.
timing_constraint: 4.5s replay before the 1st of 3 free throws.
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Showing Why a Foul Was Called While Players Walk to The Free-Throw Line
trigger_condition: A referee calls a foul on a shot attempt, stopping the clock while players walk toward the free-throw line.
editor_action: Temporarily hide the bottom scoreboard, play a slow-motion close-up showing where the defender bumped the shooter's arm or body so new viewers can see why the whistle blew, and return to the live camera before the free throw is taken.
timing_constraint: Play the slow-motion replay while players walk to the line and cut back to live action before the referee hands the ball to the shooter (example: 4.8s slow-mo replay).
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Side-By-Side Slow Motion When Referees Check The Sideline Video Monitor
trigger_condition: Referees pause the game and walk over to the sideline television monitor to review a close call (such as who touched the ball last before it went out of bounds, or whether a shot beat the buzzer).
editor_action: Show synchronized slow-motion replays from the baseline camera and the overhead basket camera zoomed in on the exact fingertips or ball release so viewers at home can judge the call right alongside the officials.
timing_constraint: Loop the clearest zoomed-in angles while the referees watch the monitor, and cut back to the live referee as soon as they step away to announce the decision (Execute within <= 1.0s reaction window and return to CAM-1 before live ball.)
plain_english_tip: Two Clocks: Teams have 30 seconds on the shot clock to hit the rim on each possession while the 20-minute half clock counts down.

title: Zooming in on The Shooter's Shoes (2-Pointer vs. 3-Pointer) and The Red Backboard Light
trigger_condition: A shooter makes a basket with their foot very close to the 3-point arc, or releases a shot right as the game clock or 30-second shot timer hits zero.
editor_action: Use a zoomed-in replay showing either (1) the shooter's sneakers to show whether their toe was touching the 3-point line (which makes the shot worth 2 points instead of 3), or (2) both the player's fingertips and the glowing red light strips on the backboard to show whether the ball left their hand before time expired.
timing_constraint: Show the zoomed-in foot-line or backboard-light angle during the next whistle pause or official review (Execute within <= 1.0s reaction window and return to CAM-1 before live ball.)
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Explaining 'Goaltending' vs. a Clean Blocked Shot in Slow Motion
trigger_condition: A defender swats a shot near the rim and the referee either counts the basket automatically ('goaltending') or waves it off as a legal block.
editor_action: In basketball, a defender can block a shot while the ball is still rising, but if they touch it after it starts coming downward toward the hoop or after it hits the backboard, it is 'goaltending' and the basket counts automatically. Roll a slow-motion side or overhead angle (REPLAY-A or CAM-5 (Above-Rim)) paused right at the peak of the shot's arc so viewers can see whether the ball was on its way down.
timing_constraint: Play the slow-motion arc verification during the next whistle pause (example: 4.5s slow-mo arc check).
plain_english_tip: Goaltending: Defenders cannot swat a shot once it is on its downward arc toward the hoop; doing so awards automatic points.

title: Double-Whistle / Conflicting Referee Calls Hold
trigger_condition: Two referees on opposite sides of the paint blow their whistles simultaneously, with one signaling a blocking foul and the other signaling a charging foul. (Visual cue: Two officials giving opposite hand signals before jogging together to confer at midcourt; Audio cue: Announcer says 'We have conflicting calls here, the officials are going to talk it over.'.)
editor_action: Hold off on displaying either 'Offensive Foul' or 'Blocking Foul' on the scorebug while the officials confer, showing the referee huddle first and then a slow-motion replay of the contact so the viewer can see why the call was split (example: suppress foul graphic until final post-conference signal). Recommended framing: Referee Conference Medium (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) -> Replay of Contact.
timing_constraint: Target window: suppress foul graphic until final post-conference signal. Cut immediately back to the crew chief when they step out of the conference to give the final ruling.
plain_english_tip: Charge vs. Block: Running into a stationary defender outside the small hoop arc is an offensive turnover ('charge').

title: Explaining 'Blocking' vs. 'Charging' Collisions in Slow Motion
trigger_condition: An offensive player driving to the hoop collides chest-to-chest with a defender, and the referee calls either a 'blocking foul' on the defense or an 'offensive foul (charge)' on the ball-handler.
editor_action: New viewers often wonder who caused a crash in the lane: play a slow-motion angle that clearly shows both the defender's feet and torso at the moment of impact so viewers can see whether the defender was already standing still in position before the driver left the floor ('a charge') or was still moving into the driver's path ('a block').
timing_constraint: Slow the replay down at the moment the driver leaves the floor and exit before the throw-in or free throw begins (example: 4.5s to 5.5s slow-mo look).
plain_english_tip: Charge vs. Block: Running into a stationary defender outside the small hoop arc is an offensive turnover ('charge').

title: Play-By-Play Excitement Pitch Trigger for Replay Hold
trigger_condition: The play-by-play announcer raises their voice pitch and volume dramatically after a spectacular highlight play. (Visual cue: A poster dunk, ankle-breaking crossover, or deep clutch three-pointer; Audio cue: Sustained high-energy vocal call from the lead announcer (e.g., 'OH WHAT A SLAM!').)
editor_action: Wait until the lead announcer finishes their peak exclamation before rolling the slow-motion replay wipe, letting the live emotion of the call land over the live hero reaction shot (example: ~2.0s post-call hold before replay wipe). Recommended framing: Tight Hero Close-Up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up).
timing_constraint: Target window: ~2.0s post-call hold before replay wipe. If the opposing team immediately pushes a fast break, cut back to CAM-1 (Main Wide) regardless of the announcer's vocal pitch.
plain_english_tip: Fast Break & Press: Sprinting to score before defenders set up, or guarding full-court immediately after a made basket.

title: 2-Point vs. 3-Point Toe-On-The-Arc Verification Replay
trigger_condition: A shooter makes a long jump shot right on the painted 3-point arc and referees signal 2 points (or review whether their toe touched the line).
editor_action: During the next dead ball, roll a zoomed-in slow-motion replay focused on the shooter's sneakers at the moment of release so viewers can see whether their toe was on the 3-point line.
timing_constraint: 3.5s zoomed foot-on-line replay on the next whistle pause.
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Showcasing Slam Dunks and Blocked Shots with Two Complementary Angles
trigger_condition: A timeout or foul pause occurs after a spectacular slam dunk, alley-oop pass caught in mid-air, or blocked shot at the rim.
editor_action: When the pause is long enough (such as a timeout or two-shot foul), play two quick angles back-to-back: start with the low baseline camera (REPLAY-A) to show how high the player jumped, then cut to the overhead rim camera (CAM-5, Above-Rim) right at impact so the viewer sees the play from above the hoop.
timing_constraint: Combine the baseline approach and overhead finish into a smooth two-angle package during extended pauses (example: 6s to 8s two-angle showcase).
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Defensive Play-Of-The-Game Package (Steals, Charges, & Dives)
trigger_condition: Macro game pattern when a team forces 3+ turnovers in a 4-minute stretch through steals, floor dives, or charges.
editor_action: Compile a 2-clip defensive hustle replay package entering the next media timeout so defense receives the same visual storytelling weight as scoring.
timing_constraint: Roll entering a media timeout after 3+ forced turnovers in 4 minutes (example: 7.5s package).
plain_english_tip: Charge vs. Block: Running into a stationary defender outside the small hoop arc is an offensive turnover ('charge').

title: No-Look / Thread-The-Needle Assist Vision Replay (Wide-To-Tight)
trigger_condition: A point guard threads a bounce pass between three defenders for a layup.
editor_action: Start the replay on a medium-wide angle at 75% speed so viewers can see the tight passing lane, rather than only showing a close-up of the layup where the pass itself is invisible.
timing_constraint: 4.5s wide-to-tight pass vision replay on the next dead ball.

title: Delayed Highlight Playback ('From Earlier' Queue When Play Stays Live)
trigger_condition: A spectacular dunk or block happens, but play continues non-stop for 60 to 90 seconds without a whistle.
editor_action: Keep the highlight saved in the Replay Buffer and roll it on the very next whistle pause with a 'From Earlier' tag so great plays are never lost during long live stretches.
timing_constraint: Hold in buffer up to 120s and roll on the next dead-ball stoppage >= 5.0s.
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Off-The-Backboard Self-Pass or Alley-Oop Replay
trigger_condition: A player throws the ball off the glass to a trailing teammate (or themselves) for a dunk.
editor_action: Roll CAM-5 (Above-Rim) or CAM-2 (Baseline Low) at 60% speed capturing the bounce off the backboard square and the mid-air catch.
timing_constraint: 4.5s slow-motion replay on the next whistle or timeout.
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Steal & Pick-Pocket Hand-Check Replay
trigger_condition: A defender pokes the ball away cleanly from a dribbler (or is whistled for a reach-in foul while trying).
editor_action: Roll a tight slow-motion replay showing whether the defender's hand struck the basketball cleanly ('all ball') or hit the dribbler's wrist.
timing_constraint: 3.5s hand-on-ball contact replay during the foul or timeout pause.

title: Star vs. Star Matchup 2-Clip Duel Package
trigger_condition: The top scorer on each team trades baskets on back-to-back possessions before a media timeout.
editor_action: Build a 2-clip 'Star Duel' replay package entering the timeout showing Player A's basket followed immediately by Player B's answer.
timing_constraint: 7.0s back-to-back duel package entering a timeout.

title: Including The Clever Pass ('Assist') Before The Basket in Highlight Replays
trigger_condition: A basket was set up by a great no-look pass, behind-the-back pass, or rapid team ball movement.
editor_action: Do not start the replay clip too late by showing only the ball going into the hoop. Start the replay a few seconds earlier ('pre-roll') so someone new to basketball can see how the passer tricked the defense and created an easy open shot for their teammate.
timing_constraint: Start the replay clip early enough to capture both the setup pass and the made basket (example: 4s to 5s pre-roll before the finish).

title: Checking Whether a Player Stepped on The Out-Of-Bounds Line
trigger_condition: A player catches a pass in the corner or dives to save a loose ball near the sideline/baseline, and the referee calls them out of bounds.
editor_action: In basketball, touching the painted boundary line with even the edge of your shoe counts as out of bounds. Roll a low-angle slow-motion replay (CAM-2 (Baseline Low) Baseline or REPLAY-B Slash) zoomed in on the player's sneakers and the boundary line during the throw-in pause.
timing_constraint: Quick zoomed-in boundary replay before the referee hands the ball to the throw-in passer (example: 3.5s to 4.5s replay).

title: Traveling Footwork Check (Pivot-Foot Drag or Extra Step)
trigger_condition: A referee calls a traveling turnover and the player or coach looks shocked at the call.
editor_action: Roll a low-angle slow-motion replay focused on the player's feet when they catch the ball or start their dribble so viewers can see the pivot-foot slide or extra step.
timing_constraint: 3.5s footwork replay if the dead-ball pause allows before the throw-in.

title: Post-Up Hook Shot / Fadeaway Separation Replay
trigger_condition: A post player or wing scores on a high-difficulty turnaround fadeaway or sky-hook over a tall defender.
editor_action: Roll a side-slash REPLAY-B angle at 65% speed showing the high release point clearing the defender's outstretched fingertips.
timing_constraint: 4.0s side-profile arc replay during the next dead ball.
plain_english_tip: The Paint: The rectangular lane under the hoop where inside scorers battle (offensive players cannot camp inside it for >3 seconds).

title: Half-Court Trap Turnover Sequence Replay (100% Speed for Context)
trigger_condition: A defensive double-team traps a ball-handler in the corner and forces an errant pass that is intercepted for a dunk.
editor_action: Play the trap and interception at 100% real-time speed before slowing to 60% on the dunk finish so viewers can see how fast the defensive rotation closed the passing lane.
timing_constraint: 100% speed trap into 60% speed finish (example: 5.0s replay).
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Over-The-Back Rebound Foul Contact Replay
trigger_condition: A rebounder jumps over the back of a defender who has established inside position ('boxed out') and is whistled for a foul.
editor_action: Roll a baseline CAM-2 (Baseline Low) replay showing the defender boxing out and the rebounder pushing their shoulders from behind.
timing_constraint: 3.5s baseline rebound-contact replay during the walk-up.
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Coach Sideline Reaction Pip / Split-Box Pairing on Big Plays
trigger_condition: A game-changing 3-pointer or turnover happens in the 2nd Half and both the play replay and the coach's reaction are compelling.
editor_action: During a full timeout, roll the play on the main replay channel and follow immediately with a 2.0s slow-motion cut of the head coach's reaction on the sideline.
timing_constraint: 4.0s highlight + 2.0s coach reaction entering a timeout.
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Then-And-Now Turnaround Packages (Showing How a Cold Shooter Caught Fire)
trigger_condition: Macro Game Pattern (Two-Half Player Turnaround): A star player who missed most of their shots in the 1st Half suddenly makes several baskets in a row in the 2nd Half.
editor_action: At the next television timeout, roll a two-part storytelling replay package that contrasts their early struggle with their second-half surge, paired with a split stat note (such as '1st Half: 1-for-7 FG | 2nd Half: 5-for-5 FG') so viewers appreciate the comeback.
timing_constraint: Roll the two-part turnaround reel entering a second-half media timeout (example: 10s to 12s highlight package).

title: Replay Wipe Whoosh Sound Effect Restraint
trigger_condition: The broadcast transitions into and out of a slow-motion replay with a graphic stinger wipe. (Visual cue: Network logo graphic sweeping across the frame for ~0.3 seconds; Audio cue: Synthetic 'whoosh' or metallic chime sound effect tied to the graphic transition.)
editor_action: Keep the transition 'whoosh' sound effect subtle and low in the mix so it acts as a gentle cue that time has shifted to a replay without startling the viewer or competing with the analyst's voice (example: -14 dB relative to commentary). Recommended framing: Replay Feed -> Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: -14 dB relative to commentary. Suppress the transition sound effect entirely during somber injury replays or official rule reviews.

title: Uniform Color Contrast Anchor on Replay Transitions
trigger_condition: A crowded scramble or rebound inside the painted area is replayed from a tight baseline camera. (Visual cue: Six to eight players in home and away jerseys tangled near the rim; Audio cue: Analyst breaking down how the offensive rebound was secured.)
editor_action: Start the replay clip half a second before the scramble begins while the key player's jersey number and team color are clearly distinguishable in open space, so the viewer can track that player into the crowd of bodies (example: ~0.6s pre-crowd lead-in on replays). Recommended framing: Baseline Close-Up Replay (CAM-2, Baseline Low).
timing_constraint: Target window: ~0.6s pre-crowd lead-in on replays. Never start a replay mid-pileup where the viewer cannot tell which limbs belong to which team.
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Match-On-Action Cut Timing for Replay Sequences
trigger_condition: A highlight replay is shown from two sequential camera angles during a timeout or review (e.g., baseline angle followed by rim angle). (Visual cue: Player rising toward the basket for a dunk or block; Audio cue: Analyst narrating the replay sequence.)
editor_action: When chaining two replay angles of the same play, either let the first angle finish completely before starting the second, or overlap the action by ~0.5 seconds so the viewer's brain can smoothly anchor the exact moment of the jump across the two viewpoints (example: 0.5s action overlap on multi-angle replay). Recommended framing: Baseline Replay (CAM-2, Baseline Low) -> Under-Basket Replay (CAM-5, Above-Rim).
timing_constraint: Target window: 0.5s action overlap on multi-angle replay. Never cut between two replay angles mid-air without either a clean match-on-action or a distinct replay transition wipe.
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Color Analyst Breakdown Cut to Target Player
trigger_condition: During a free-throw routine or dead ball, the color analyst begins praising or critiquing a specific player's mechanics or footwork. (Visual cue: Game clock is stopped while players line up along the free-throw lane; Audio cue: Analyst mentions a specific player's name and technique (e.g., 'Watch how he sets his feet on the catch...').)
editor_action: Cut to an isolated camera on the player being discussed or roll a quick clip of their recent footwork so the visual picture illustrates the analyst's spoken lesson (example: cut within ~1.2s of named breakdown). Recommended framing: Tight Hero Close-Up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) or Replay Clip.
timing_constraint: Return to the free-throw shooter before the referee hands them the ball for the live attempt.
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: LED-Stanchion / Digital Ad-Board Flicker Mitigation
trigger_condition: A high-frame-rate super-slow-motion replay camera shows noticeable strobing or banding on the courtside LED advertising boards. (Visual cue: Flickering horizontal bands on background LED ribbons during slow-motion playback; Audio cue: Replay commentary.)
editor_action: If a super-slow-motion angle exhibits severe LED refresh strobing that distracts from the player action, prefer an alternate camera angle looking downward toward the wood floor or play the clip at 50%-75% speed where flicker is minimized (example: select low-flicker angle when LED strobing exceeds comfort threshold). Recommended framing: Alternative Replay Angle (CAM-2 (Baseline Low) or CAM-5 (Above-Rim)).
timing_constraint: Target window: select low-flicker angle when LED strobing exceeds comfort threshold. Always prioritize clear visibility of the ball and players over slow-motion speed.

title: Dual-Analyst Cross-Talk Prevention on Three-Person Booths
trigger_condition: A broadcast features a play-by-play announcer and two color analysts, and both analysts begin speaking at the same time after a stoppage. (Visual cue: A replay clip rolling during a timeout or foul stoppage; Audio cue: Overlapping speech energy detected on Analyst Mic 1 and Analyst Mic 2.)
editor_action: Hold the current visual replay clip steady rather than cutting rapidly while the analysts yield the floor to one another, ensuring visual calm while the audio settles (example: maintain current camera for at least ~2.5s when dual-analyst speech overlaps). Recommended framing: Replay Feed or Booth Camera.
timing_constraint: Target window: maintain current camera for at least ~2.5s when dual-analyst speech overlaps. Play-by-play microphone always retains top priority if live action resumes on the court.

title: Moving Screen (Illegal Offensive Pick) Contact Replay
trigger_condition: An offensive screener is whistled for an illegal moving screen away from the basket.
editor_action: Roll a medium slow-motion replay focused on the screener's hips and feet still moving as they collide with the defender.
timing_constraint: 3.5s screen-contact replay during the turnover handoff if pause >= 5.0s.
plain_english_tip: Screen (Pick): An offensive teammate stands still to block a defender and create open space, then cuts ('rolls') toward the hoop.

title: Bank-Shot or Lucky Bounce Rim-Roll Replay
trigger_condition: A shot bounces high off the rim three or four times ('shooter's roll') or banks in unexpectedly at a key moment.
editor_action: Roll the overhead CAM-5 (Above-Rim) angle during the next dead ball so viewers can watch the ball bounce around the iron and drop through the net.
timing_constraint: 3.5s CAM-5 rim-bounce replay on the next stoppage.
